```{python}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
import os, sys, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
from matplotlib import colors as _mc

def find_repo_root(start, marker="lib"):
    p = os.path.abspath(start)
    while True:
        if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(p, marker)):
            return p
        parent = os.path.dirname(p)
        if parent == p:
            raise FileNotFoundError("No lib folder found above " + str(start))
        p = parent

REPO = find_repo_root(os.getcwd())
sys.path.append(os.path.join(REPO, "lib"))

from python_style_util import p, f, s, C
from credit_utils.eda import default_rate_by_bin
from deck_utils import (deck_style, BRAND_RAMP, add_baseline,
                        strip_bar_labels, small_labels, reset_labels)
deck_style()

plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 13, "axes.titlesize": 16, "axes.labelsize": 14,
                     "xtick.labelsize": 13, "ytick.labelsize": 13, "legend.fontsize": 13})

def card(num, label, note="", num_size=56, colour="#3D2E4F"):
    n = f"<div style='font-family:monospace;font-size:{num_size}px;font-weight:700;color:{colour};line-height:1.05'>{num}</div>"
    l = f"<div style='font-size:15px;letter-spacing:0.06em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#8A6D1F;margin-top:10px'>{label}</div>"
    t = f"<div style='font-size:16px;color:#3a3a3a;margin-top:4px'>{note}</div>" if note else ""
    return f"<div>{n}{l}{t}</div>"

def grid(items, cols):
    return ("<div style='display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(%d,1fr);gap:28px;margin-top:20px'>" % cols
            + "".join(items) + "</div>")

def pretty(name):
    return DISPLAY.get(name, name.replace("_", " ").title())

DATA = os.path.join(REPO, "Datasets", "Home Credit Default Risk", "application_train.csv")
IV_FILE = os.path.join(REPO, "01_Default_Rate_Driver_Scan_EDA", "iv_screen.csv")
IV_CUTOFF = 0.02   # project drop threshold (Siddiqi band). Confirm against notebook section 5.

# Display names shared with the Stage 02 and Stage 04 decks
DISPLAY = {
    "EXT_SOURCE_1": "External Credit Score 1", "EXT_SOURCE_2": "External Credit Score 2",
    "EXT_SOURCE_3": "External Credit Score 3", "DAYS_EMPLOYED": "Job Tenure",
    "EMP_YEARS": "Job Tenure", "AGE_YEARS": "Age", "EMPLOYED_AGE": "Employed-to-Age Ratio",
    "ANNUITY_CREDIT": "Annuity-to-Credit Ratio", "AMT_GOODS_PRICE": "Goods Price",
    "AMT_CREDIT": "Loan Amount", "AMT_INCOME_TOTAL": "Income", "AMT_ANNUITY": "Annuity",
    "CREDIT_GOODS": "Credit-to-Goods Ratio (LVR)", "DTI": "Debt-to-Income Ratio",
    "OCCUPATION_TYPE": "Occupation", "ORG_BAND": "Organisation Band",
    "NAME_INCOME_TYPE": "Income Type", "REGION_RATING_CLIENT_W_CITY": "Regional Rating",
    "NAME_EDUCATION_TYPE": "Education",
}

usecols = ["TARGET", "EXT_SOURCE_1", "EXT_SOURCE_2", "EXT_SOURCE_3",
           "DAYS_BIRTH", "DAYS_EMPLOYED", "NAME_EDUCATION_TYPE", "CNT_CHILDREN",
           "AMT_INCOME_TOTAL", "AMT_CREDIT", "AMT_ANNUITY", "AMT_GOODS_PRICE", "CODE_GENDER"]
raw = pd.read_csv(DATA, usecols=usecols)
N_ALL = len(raw)                      # 307,511 applications
BASE = raw["TARGET"].mean()           # 8.07% across all applications

df = raw[raw["CODE_GENDER"] != "XNA"].copy()   # 4 rows with XNA gender dropped for charts
df["DAYS_EMPLOYED"] = df["DAYS_EMPLOYED"].replace(365243, np.nan)
df["AGE_YEARS"] = -df["DAYS_BIRTH"] / 365.25
df["EMP_YEARS"] = -df["DAYS_EMPLOYED"] / 365.25

def _sd(n, d): return n / d.replace(0, np.nan)
df["DTI"]          = _sd(df["AMT_ANNUITY"], df["AMT_INCOME_TOTAL"])
df["CREDIT_GOODS"] = _sd(df["AMT_CREDIT"],  df["AMT_GOODS_PRICE"])
df["EMPLOYED_AGE"] = _sd(df["DAYS_EMPLOYED"], df["DAYS_BIRTH"])
```

## The Short Version {.hero data-kick="Executive summary"}

::: {.hero-wrap}
::: {.hero-col}
<div class="hero-num">`{python} f"{BASE:.2%}"`<small>repayment difficulty across all applications</small></div>
:::

::: {.hero-col}
Across **307,511 applications**, three groups of fields separate applicants by risk:

- **External credit scores:** the strongest separation
- **Age and job tenure:** younger applicants and shorter job tenure default more
- **Affordability ratios:** repayment size relative to income and loan value

Raw loan amount shows no clear pattern on its own.
:::
:::

Driver performance is compared with the `{python} f"{BASE:.2%}"` portfolio default rate.

## Dataset Overview {data-kick="The data"}

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.0
#| out-width: "90%"
counts = raw["TARGET"].value_counts(normalize=True).sort_index()
labels = ["TARGET = 0: Repaid", "TARGET = 1: Repayment difficulty"]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 3.4))
bars = ax.barh(labels, counts.values, color=[p("jacaranda", 300), p("gold", 300)],
               alpha=0.95, edgecolor="white", linewidth=1.2, height=0.62)
for b, v in zip(bars, counts.values):
    ax.text(v + 0.012, b.get_y() + b.get_height()/2, f"{v:.2%}", va="center",
            fontweight="bold", fontfamily=f("mono"), fontsize=12, color=C.text)
ax.set_xlim(0, 1); ax.set_xlabel("Share of applications")
ax.set_title(f"{N_ALL:,} applications, 122 fields, {BASE:.2%} repayment difficulty", loc="left")
ax.grid(axis="x"); ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.invert_yaxis()
plt.show()
```

**Class imbalance:** repayment difficulty affects 8.07% of applications, about 11 repaid applications for every one with difficulty. Each group is therefore read against the 8.07% line.

## How to Read the Charts {data-kick="Method"}

Each bar is a group's repayment-difficulty rate, compared with the **`{python} f"{BASE:.2%}"` portfolio rate** (dashed line).

```{python}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.9
ex = df.assign(kids=df["CNT_CHILDREN"].clip(upper=3)).groupby("kids")["TARGET"].mean()
ex.index = ["0 children", "1 child", "2 children", "3 or more"]
norm = _mc.Normalize(ex.min(), ex.max())
rgba = BRAND_RAMP(norm(ex.values)); rgba[:, 3] = 0.95
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 3.9))
bars = ax.bar(ex.index, ex.values, color=rgba, edgecolor="white", linewidth=1.0, width=0.55)
ax.axhline(BASE, ls="--", color=C.text_muted, lw=1.4)
ax.text(3.45, BASE, f" portfolio {BASE:.2%}", va="bottom", ha="right", fontsize=13,
        color=C.text_muted, fontfamily=f("mono"))
ax.bar_label(bars, labels=[f"{v:.1%}" for v in ex.values], padding=4, fontweight="bold",
             fontfamily=f("mono"), fontsize=14, color=C.text)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1))
ax.set_ylim(0, ex.max() * 1.2)
ax.tick_params(labelsize=14)
ax.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
plt.show()
```

Lighter = lower repayment difficulty, darker = higher. **Bars that move away from the line show separation; bars close to it show little.**

## External Credit Scores {data-kick="Signal"}

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| out-width: "100%"
fig, axes = default_rate_by_bin(
    df, ["EXT_SOURCE_2", "EXT_SOURCE_3", "EXT_SOURCE_1"],
    target="TARGET", ncols=3, bins=10, bin_label="rank",
    grade_scale=BRAND_RAMP, na_as_bin=True, panel_w=3.7, panel_h=3.3,
    show_base_rate=False,
)
strip_bar_labels(axes)
for ax in np.ravel(np.asarray(axes)):
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1))
add_baseline(axes, BASE)
plt.show()
```

**External credit scores show the strongest separation in default rates among the screened variables.**

## Age and Job Tenure {data-kick="Signal"}

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| out-width: "100%"
small_labels(9)
fig, axes = default_rate_by_bin(
    df, ["AGE_YEARS", "EMP_YEARS"], target="TARGET",
    ncols=2, bins=8, method="quantile", bin_label="range",
    grade_scale=BRAND_RAMP, na_as_bin=True, panel_w=5.5, panel_h=3.4,
    show_base_rate=False,
)
reset_labels()
add_baseline(axes, BASE)
plt.show()
```

**Default rates are higher among younger applicants and those with shorter job tenure.** The missing job-tenure bin is pensioners, whose rate is low.

## Education {data-kick="Signal"}

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| out-width: "100%"
order = df.groupby("NAME_EDUCATION_TYPE")["TARGET"].mean().sort_values()
norm = _mc.Normalize(order.min(), order.max())
rgba = BRAND_RAMP(norm(order.values)); rgba[:, 3] = 0.95
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 4.4))
bars = ax.barh(order.index.astype(str), order.values, color=rgba,
               edgecolor="white", linewidth=1.0)
ax.axvline(BASE, ls="--", color=C.text_muted, lw=1, zorder=1.4)
ax.text(BASE, len(order) - 0.35, f" portfolio {BASE:.2%}", va="bottom", ha="left",
        fontsize=11, color=C.text_muted, fontfamily=f("mono"), zorder=5,
        bbox=dict(facecolor="white", edgecolor="none", boxstyle="round,pad=0.18", alpha=0.85))
for b, v in zip(bars, order.values):
    ax.text(v + 0.002, b.get_y() + b.get_height()/2, f"{v:.1%}", va="center",
            fontweight="bold", fontsize=12, fontfamily=f("mono"), color=C.text)
ax.set_xlim(0, order.values.max() * 1.16)
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1))
ax.set_title("Default rate by education level", loc="left")
ax.grid(axis="x"); ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"Default rates rise as education level falls, from **{order.iloc[0]:.1%}** for "
      f"{order.index[0].lower()} to **{order.iloc[-1]:.1%}** for {order.index[-1].lower()}.")
```

## Loan Amount {data-kick="Signal"}

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| out-width: "100%"
fig, axes = default_rate_by_bin(
    df, ["AMT_CREDIT", "AMT_INCOME_TOTAL", "AMT_ANNUITY"],
    target="TARGET", ncols=3, bins=10, bin_label="rank",
    grade_scale=BRAND_RAMP, panel_w=3.7, panel_h=3.3, show_base_rate=False,
)
strip_bar_labels(axes)
for ax in np.ravel(np.asarray(axes)):
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1))
add_baseline(axes, BASE)
plt.show()
```

**Default rate does not show a clear monotonic relationship with loan amount.**

## Affordability Ratios {data-kick="Signal"}

<div style="font-size:18px">LVR = loan ÷ goods price · Employed-to-Age = job tenure ÷ age · Debt-to-Income = annuity ÷ income</div>

```{python}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| out-width: "100%"
fig, axes = default_rate_by_bin(
    df, ["EMPLOYED_AGE", "CREDIT_GOODS", "DTI"], target="TARGET",
    ncols=3, bins=12, bin_label="rank", grade_scale=BRAND_RAMP, na_as_bin=True,
    panel_w=3.7, panel_h=3.3, show_base_rate=False,
)
strip_bar_labels(axes)   # 12 near-equal bins: labels collide, so the y-axis carries values
for ax in np.ravel(np.asarray(axes)):
    ax.margins(y=0.06)
add_baseline(axes, BASE)
plt.show()
```

**Employed-to-Age and LVR separate risk across groups. Debt-to-Income shows no clear pattern.**

## WOE and Information Value {data-kick="Feature selection"}

```{python}
#| output: asis
if os.path.exists(IV_FILE):
    iv_tbl = pd.read_csv(IV_FILE).sort_values("iv", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)
    n_total = len(iv_tbl)
    print("| Feature | Information Value | Decision |")
    print("|---|---:|---|")
    for _, r in iv_tbl.head(12).iterrows():
        d = "Retained" if r["iv"] >= IV_CUTOFF else "Not retained"
        print(f"| {pretty(r['feature'])} | {r['iv']:.3f} | {d} |")
    print(f"\nTop 12 of {n_total} screened features. **IV cutoff: {IV_CUTOFF:.2f}.** Features above the cutoff move forward to logistic model development.")
else:
    print("::: {.caveat}\nIV table pending. Export `iv_screen.csv` (columns `feature`, `iv`) from notebook section 5.3 into this project folder, then re-render.\n:::")
```
